title: Update apart from draw
description:
Split a tiny game into an `update` that changes the state and a `draw` that only describes what to show:

```cpp
struct Input { bool left; bool right; bool pausePressed; };
struct Game { float x{ 100 }; bool paused{ false }; int frames{ 0 }; };

void update(Game& g, const Input& in);
std::vector<std::string> draw(const Game& g);
```

**update**
- `pausePressed` toggles `paused`, always.
- While paused, nothing else changes.
- Otherwise: `right` adds 4 to `x`, `left` subtracts 4 (both: no movement); `x` stays within `0..750`; `frames` goes up by one.

**draw** returns the draw calls in order, as text:
1. `"clear RAYWHITE"`
2. `"rect <x> 200 50 50"` with `x` as a whole number (truncated, like `static_cast<int>`)
3. `"text frames <frames>"`
4. and only while paused, last: `"text PAUSED"`
hints: Toggle the pause first, then `return` early while paused.
